mainTopic: When קידושין takes effect with forbidden women (עריות, נדה, לאוין) and the views of רבי עקיבא and the רבנן, and why it never works with a שפחה כנענית
overview: The גמרא has learned that קידושין does not work with the עריות, because they are all compared to אחות אשה. It asks why נדה is different, and חזקיה answers from a פסוק. It also explains that when a comparison could go either way, we choose the stricter one. רב אחא בר יעקב offers another source, a קל וחומר from a יבמה. רב פפא then shows from the 'loved wife and hated wife' פסוק that קידושין does work with women forbidden only by a לאו. The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא, who disagrees, explains that פסוק. It works through the reports of רבי סימאי and רבי ישבב and admits that רבי עקיבא's reading is forced. Finally, רב הונא learns from 'stay here with the donkey' that קידושין does not work with a שפחה כנענית. The גמרא then begins to ask where we learn that her child follows her status, and that question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why is נדה not included with the other עריות?
steps.stepSummary: If all עריות are compared to אחות אשה, then קידושין should also fail with a נדה. But אביי said everyone agrees a child born from a נדה is not a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the same should apply to a נדה! Why then did אביי say that everyone agrees a child from a נדה or a סוטה is not a ממזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the comparison of all עריות to אחות אשה. A נדה is listed among the עריות, so the comparison should make her the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison should mean that קידושין fails with a נדה and that her child is a ממזר. But אביי states that all agree the child of a נדה is not a ממזר. So there is a contradiction between the comparison and אביי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her state of menstrual impurity
A wife forbidden to her husband because she is suspected of being unfaithful
A child born from a forbidden union where קידושין cannot take effect
Why then? (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: Then even a menstruating woman as well!
phrases.notes: He means: by the same comparison, קידושין with a נדה should not work either.

phrases.english: Why then did Abaye say:
All agree regarding one who has relations with a menstruating woman
or with a sotah, that the child is not a mamzer?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ נִדָּה נָמֵי! אַלְּמָה אָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comparison of all עריות to אחות אשה, which was taught just before this section
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of all עריות to אחות אשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: נדה is one of the עריות, so the comparison should block her קידושין. Yet אביי rules her child is not a ממזר.

steps.title: A פסוק shows that marriage works with a נדה
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה learns from the word 'ותהי' that a נדה can still be married, so she is an exception to the comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: The פסוק says 'And her impurity shall be upon him.' This teaches that even while she is a נדה, marriage can take effect with her.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers the question by bringing a special פסוק that teaches that נדה is an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'ותהי' comes from the same root as 'הויה', the Torah's word for becoming someone's wife. So the Torah hints that a נדה can still 'become' a wife. She stays among the forbidden relations, but קידושין with her works.

keyTerms.meaning: And it shall be
'Becoming' a wife; taking effect of marriage

phrases.english: Chizkiyah said: The verse states
"And her impurity shall be upon him,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:24

phrases.english: even at the time of her impurity
there can be 'becoming' with her.
phrases.notes: 'ותהי' and 'הויה' come from the same root, and the Torah uses 'הויה' for getting married (דברים 24:2).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from נדה
steps.terutzResolutionType: A special פסוק makes נדה an exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: נדה should be like all other עריות, with no קידושין
steps.terutzMaskana: A פסוק teaches that קידושין works with a נדה
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why a child born to a נדה is not a ממזר.

steps.title: Why compare the עריות to אחות אשה and not to נדה?
steps.stepSummary: Two comparisons are possible, one to נדה (where marriage works) and one to אחות אשה (where it doesn't). Why choose אחות אשה?
steps.simpleTranslation: Now, we could compare the other עריות to נדה, and we could compare them to אחות אשה. What made you compare them to אחות אשה? Compare them to נדה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks a new question. Since the Torah shows that marriage works with a נדה, maybe all the עריות should follow her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נדה and אחות אשה both appear in the same list of עריות. One gives a lenient result (marriage works) and one gives a strict result (marriage fails). The גמרא asks what decides which one we follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, after all (opens an argument)
To compare by a היקש
What did you see? Why choose this option over the other?
A wife's sister

phrases.english: Now, it is possible to compare them to a menstruating woman,
phrases.notes: 'Them' is the rest of the עריות.

phrases.english: and it is possible to compare them to a wife's sister;

phrases.aramaic: מַאי חָזֵית דְּמַקְּשַׁתְּ לְהוּ לַאֲחוֹת אִשָּׁה?
phrases.english: what did you see that you compare them to a wife's sister?
Compare them to a menstruating woman!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on חזקיה's answer to question the choice of comparison
steps.kashyaTarget: The choice of אחות אשה as the model for all עריות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both נדה and אחות אשה could serve as the model. Choosing one over the other needs a reason.

steps.title: When in doubt, we compare toward the stricter result
steps.stepSummary: When a comparison could go either the lenient way or the strict way, we go the strict way.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the choice is between a leniency and a stringency, we compare toward the stringency.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a rule: we follow the stricter comparison. So the עריות are compared to אחות אשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing to נדה would let marriage work with all עריות, which is lenient. Comparing to אחות אשה blocks marriage, which is strict. So we choose אחות אשה, and נדה remains the one exception.

keyTerms.meaning: A leniency
A stringency
We compare (by היקש)

steps.whatToRemember: All עריות are compared to אחות אשה, so קידושין fails with them. נדה is an exception because of a special פסוק.

phrases.english: A leniency and a stringency:
we compare toward the stringency.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers why the comparison is to אחות אשה
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general rule for choosing between two possible comparisons
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We could just as well compare the עריות to נדה
steps.terutzMaskana: We choose the comparison that leads to the stricter result

steps.title: A קל וחומר from יבמה
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב gives a different source. קידושין does not work with a יבמה, who is forbidden only by a לאו, so surely it does not work with women forbidden by מיתה or כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: We learn it by a קל וחומר from a יבמה. A יבמה is forbidden only by a לאו, and still קידושין does not work with her. Surely it does not work with women forbidden by מיתה or כרת!
steps.whatsHappening: Here a different אמורא gives a new source for the rule that קידושין fails with עריות. He does not use the comparison to אחות אשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יבמה waiting for יבום is forbidden to other men only by a לאו, which is a lighter prohibition. Yet another man's קידושין with her does not work. If this is true for a lighter prohibition, it must be true for the heavier prohibitions of מיתה and כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a heavier one
A widow waiting for יבום or חליצה from her late husband's brother
A negative commandment, punished by lashes
קידושין takes effect
Relations punished by death or by כרת

phrases.english: Rav Acha bar Ya'akov said:
It is derived by an a fortiori argument from a yevama:
Just as a yevama, who is forbidden by a mere prohibition,
betrothal does not take effect with her,
those liable to death and those liable to karet,
is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: אָתְיָא בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר מִיבָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין fails with women forbidden by מיתה or כרת, learned by קל וחומר from יבמה

steps.title: Then marriage should fail with every לאו
steps.stepSummary: If even a לאו blocks קידושין with a יבמה, then it should block קידושין with every woman forbidden by a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the same should apply to all other women forbidden by a לאו!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר יעקב's source. His proof seems to go too far.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His proof starts from a case where a mere לאו stops קידושין. That seems to show that any לאו should stop קידושין. But marriage with a woman forbidden only by a לאו is generally valid.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Relations forbidden by a לאו

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, שְׁאָר חַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין נָמֵי!
phrases.english: If so, other prohibitions should also apply!
phrases.notes: He means: קידושין should also fail with all other women forbidden by a לאו.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, שְׁאָר חַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב אחא בר יעקב's קל וחומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a לאו blocks קידושין for a יבמה, then every לאו should block קידושין.

steps.title: The Torah says marriage works with a לאו
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא brings the פסוק about a loved wife and a hated wife. The 'hated' wife is one forbidden by a לאו, and the Torah still calls her his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: For women forbidden by a לאו, the Torah says it openly: 'If a man has two wives, one loved and one hated.' Is anyone hated or loved by ה׳? Rather, 'loved' means loved in her marriage, which is permitted. 'Hated' means hated in her marriage, because it breaks a לאו. And the Torah still says 'If a man has' them as wives.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that a פסוק shows marriage works with women forbidden by a לאו. So the יבמה case cannot be extended to every לאו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ does not truly hate any person, so 'hated' must describe a marriage that is forbidden by a לאו. The Torah still says 'תהיין', meaning both women are his wives. This shows that קידושין works with women forbidden by a regular לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: Explicitly
Loved
Hated
Before ה׳
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: קידושין does not work with women forbidden by מיתה or כרת, except נדה. It does work with women forbidden only by a לאו, as the פסוק of the 'hated wife' shows.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Regarding those forbidden by a prohibition, it is written explicitly:
"If a man has two wives,
phrases.notes: דברים 21:15

phrases.english: the one loved and the one hated."
But is there one who is hated before the Omnipresent
and one who is loved before the Omnipresent?
Rather, "loved" means loved in her marriage,
"hated" means hated in her marriage.
phrases.notes: Her marriage is 'hated' because it breaks a לאו.

phrases.english: And the Merciful One says: "If a man has" them.
phrases.notes: The Torah calls both of them his wives, so the forbidden marriage still counts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: חַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין בְּהֶדְיָא כְּתִיב בְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge that every לאו should block קידושין
steps.terutzResolutionType: An explicit פסוק excludes ordinary לאוים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Based on the יבמה case, any לאו should block קידושין
steps.terutzMaskana: A פסוק shows that קידושין works with a woman forbidden by a regular לאו
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why marriages that break only a לאו are still valid marriages.

steps.title: How does רבי עקיבא explain the hated-wife verse?
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that קידושין does not work with women forbidden by a לאו. So what does the פסוק about a 'hated' wife mean for him?
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי עקיבא, who says that betrothal does not take effect with women forbidden by a לאו, how does he explain the פסוק 'If a man has two wives'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's reading from step 7. According to רבי עקיבא, the 'hated' wife cannot be a woman forbidden by a לאו, so what case does the פסוק describe?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 said the 'hated' wife is a woman forbidden by a לאו, and the Torah still calls her his wife. But רבי עקיבא holds that קידושין never works with such a woman. So he must explain the פסוק as some other case where קידושין does work.

keyTerms.meaning: Women a man is forbidden to marry by a negative commandment (a לאו)
The betrothal 'takes hold', meaning it is valid
He explains it as referring to (a certain case)

phrases.english: And according to רבי עקיבא, who says:
Betrothal does not take effect with women forbidden by a לאו,
"If there will be" — what case does he say it is about?
phrases.notes: דברים 21:15, the פסוק about a man with two wives, one loved and one hated, from step 7.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's reading of the פסוק from the view of רבי עקיבא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's reading that the 'hated' wife is one forbidden by a לאו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי עקיבא holds that קידושין does not work with women forbidden by a לאו, so for him the פסוק cannot mean that. He needs another case.

steps.title: The verse is about a widow married to a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא explains the 'hated' wife as a widow married to a כהן גדול, following רבי סימאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: He explains it as a widow married to a כהן גדול, following the opinion of רבי סימאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי עקיבא reads the פסוק as a widow married to a כהן גדול. The next step brings רבי סימאי's teaching to back this up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A widow is forbidden to a כהן גדול, yet according to רבי סימאי, רבי עקיבא treats this case differently from other forbidden unions. Because קידושין still works there, the Torah can call her 'his wife'.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow married to a כהן גדול, which the Torah forbids

phrases.english: It is about a widow married to a כהן גדול,
and this follows רבי סימאי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by naming a specific case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבי עקיבא, the 'hated' wife has no case to describe, since קידושין fails with all women forbidden by a לאו
steps.terutzMaskana: For רבי עקיבא, the פסוק describes a widow married to a כהן גדול, where קידושין does work according to רבי סימאי

steps.title: רבי סימאי's teaching about רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: רבי סימאי says רבי עקיבא made the child a ממזר in all forbidden unions except a widow with a כהן גדול, because the Torah calls that child a חלל, not a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי סימאי says: In every forbidden union, רבי עקיבא would make the child a ממזר, except for a widow married to a כהן גדול. That is because the Torah says 'He shall not profane', which means he makes his children חללים, not ממזרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that supports step 9. It shows that רבי עקיבא treated a widow with a כהן גדול as a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, a child is a ממזר whenever קידושין cannot work. Since the Torah says the child of a widow and a כהן גדול is only a חלל and not a ממזר, קידושין must work in that case. This is why the 'hated' wife can be her.

keyTerms.meaning: A child born from a forbidden union who may not marry a regular Jew
'He shall not profane', the Torah's words about a כהן גדול who marries a widow
Making the children חללים, meaning they lose כהונה status but are not ממזרים

steps.confusionAlert: A חלל is not the same as a ממזר. A חלל only loses the special status of a כהן; a ממזר cannot marry into the regular Jewish community.

phrases.english: As it is taught: רבי סימאי says:

phrases.aramaic: מִן הַכֹּל הָיָה רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא עוֹשֶׂה מַמְזֵר
phrases.english: In all forbidden unions, רבי עקיבא would make the child a ממזר,
except for a widow married to a כהן גדול,
since the Torah said: "He shall not profane":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 21:15

phrases.english: he makes them חללים,
but he does not make them ממזרים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the ברייתא that supports the answer in step 9
steps.raayaObject: That according to רבי עקיבא, קידושין works with a widow married to a כהן גדול
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי סימאי in a ברייתא, based on the words לא יחלל

steps.title: What about רבי ישבב's version of רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישבב reports that רבי עקיבא made the child a ממזר in every forbidden union, with no exception. How does that fit?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what about רבי ישבב, who says: Come, let us cry out against עקיבא בן יוסף, who used to say: Whenever a man may not marry a woman in Israel, the child is a ממזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem. רבי ישבב says רבי עקיבא made the child a ממזר in every forbidden union, so the widow with a כהן גדול would not be an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9's answer depended on רבי סימאי saying a widow with a כהן גדול is an exception. רבי ישבב seems to say there is no exception at all. If so, the 'hated' wife again has no case to describe for רבי עקיבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us cry out (in protest)
A woman he is not allowed to be with in Israel, meaning any forbidden union

phrases.english: And according to רבי ישבב, who says:

phrases.aramaic: בּוֹאוּ וְנִצְוַוח עַל עֲקִיבָא בֶּן יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: Come, let us cry out against עקיבא בן יוסף,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהָיָה אוֹמֵר: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בִּיאָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל –
phrases.english: who used to say: whenever a man may not be with that woman in Israel,
the child is a ממזר?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer from step 9 using a different report of רבי עקיבא's view
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that רבי עקיבא reads the פסוק as a widow married to a כהן גדול
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ישבב reports that רבי עקיבא made the child a ממזר in every forbidden union, which leaves no exception for a widow with a כהן גדול

steps.title: Fine if רבי ישבב is only arguing with רבי סימאי
steps.stepSummary: If רבי ישבב only means to reject רבי סימאי's exception, there is no problem. The פסוק can be about women forbidden by an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for רבי ישבב if he is coming to reject רבי סימאי's view. Then it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one way out. If רבי ישבב is only arguing with רבי סימאי about the widow with a כהן גדול, the question can be answered. This step sets up the 'but if' in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, רבי ישבב only adds the widow-with-כהן-גדול case to the ממזר list. Women forbidden by an עשה are still not included, so קידושין works with them. Then the 'hated' wife can be a woman forbidden by an עשה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This works well', introducing a case where there is no problem
To exclude, meaning to argue against
Fine, good

phrases.english: This works well according to רבי ישבב
if he is coming to reject the view of רבי סימאי;
phrases.notes: He would only be disagreeing about the widow with a כהן גדול, not adding every kind of forbidden woman.

phrases.english: then it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a partial answer to step 11 before the challenge returns in step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting how far רבי ישבב's statement reaches
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי ישבב's report leaves no case where קידושין works for רבי עקיבא
steps.terutzMaskana: If רבי ישבב only rejects רבי סימאי's exception, women forbidden by an עשה are still a possible case for the פסוק

steps.title: But if רבי ישבב states a full rule of his own
steps.stepSummary: If רבי ישבב means that רבי עקיבא made the child a ממזר even with women forbidden by an עשה, what case is left for the פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he is stating his own reasoning, and it includes even women forbidden by an עשה, what case does he say the פסוק is about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sharpens the challenge. If רבי ישבב means that even women forbidden by an עשה make a ממזר for רבי עקיבא, then no case seems left for the 'hated' wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this reading, רבי ישבב is not just arguing about one case. He is saying רבי עקיבא held that every forbidden union, even one forbidden only by an עשה, gives a ממזר. Then קידושין never works with any forbidden woman, and the question 'what case is the פסוק about?' comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: His own reasoning, meaning a statement that stands on its own
Women forbidden by a positive commandment (an עשה)

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא, the 'hated' wife must be a case where קידושין still works. According to רבי סימאי, that is a widow with a כהן גדול. According to a narrow reading of רבי ישבב, it is a woman forbidden by an עשה. If רבי ישבב includes even women forbidden by an עשה, the next step gives the remaining case.

phrases.english: But if he is stating a reasoning of his own,
which includes even women forbidden by an עשה,
what case does he say it is about?
phrases.notes: "It" is the פסוק about the hated wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings back the challenge for the broader reading of רבי ישבב
steps.kashyaTarget: Explaining the 'hated' wife according to רבי עקיבא as רבי ישבב reports him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If even women forbidden by an עשה make a ממזר for רבי עקיבא, then קידושין fails with every forbidden woman, and no case is left for the פסוק

steps.title: רבי ישבב's case: a non-virgin married to a כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: According to רבי ישבב, the 'hated wife' in the פסוק is a בעולה married to a כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק is talking about a woman who is not a virgin, married to a כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 13. Even if, as רבי ישבב reports him, רבי עקיבא makes a ממזר from women forbidden by an עשה, one case is still left for the פסוק: a בעולה with a כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול has a positive command to marry a בתולה, so marrying a בעולה breaks an עשה. Even in רבי ישבב's report of רבי עקיבא, this child is not a ממזר, so this marriage works. That is why it can be the 'hated wife' in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is no longer a virgin
The High Priest

phrases.english: With a non-virgin married to a High Priest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by naming a case that is still left for the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a remaining case that fits the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If every עשה creates a ממזר for רבי עקיבא, as רבי ישבב reports him, no case is left for the פסוק.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case of a בעולה with a כהן גדול is still left, because there the child is not a ממזר.

steps.title: Why is this positive command different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a בעולה with a כהן גדול is different from other unions forbidden by an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If other unions forbidden by an עשה make a ממזר, why not this one?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן גדול with a בעולה also breaks an עשה. So if רבי עקיבא, as רבי ישבב reports him, makes the child a ממזר in other עשה cases, it seems he should do the same here.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the difference?

phrases.english: And what is different?
phrases.notes: He means: why is this עשה different from the other ones, where רבי עקיבא (as רבי ישבב reports him) makes the child a ממזר?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a בעולה with a כהן גדול does not create a ממזר for רבי עקיבא, as רבי ישבב reports him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It is also an עשה, so it should be like all the other עשה cases.

steps.title: A positive command that does not apply to everyone
steps.stepSummary: This עשה applies only to the כהן גדול, so it is treated as less severe.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because it is a positive command that does not apply equally to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 15. This עשה is different because it only applies to one person, the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most עשה prohibitions on marriage apply to every Jew. The rule about a בתולה applies only to the כהן גדול, so it carries less weight, and the child is not a ממזר.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive command
A positive command that does not apply equally to everyone

phrases.english: Because it is
a positive command that is not equal for all.
phrases.notes: Only the כהן גדול must marry a בתולה. Other people, even regular כהנים, may marry a בעולה.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵי לֵיהּ עֲשֵׂה שֶׁאֵין שָׁוֶה בַּכֹּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All עשה prohibitions are the same, so this one should also create a ממזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: An עשה that applies only to the כהן גדול is weaker, so the child is not a ממזר.
steps.whatToRemember: In רבי ישבב's report of רבי עקיבא, the 'hated wife' is a בעולה married to a כהן גדול. This works because that עשה does not apply to everyone.

steps.title: Why don't the רבנן use positive-command cases?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן place the פסוק in cases forbidden by a לאו instead of cases forbidden by an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן: instead of explaining the פסוק as women forbidden by a לאו, let them explain it as women forbidden by an עשה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן, who argue with רבי עקיבא. It asks why they did not explain the 'hated wife' as a woman forbidden only by an עשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן use the פסוק to show that קידושין work with women forbidden by a לאו. The גמרא suggests they could read it as a case forbidden by an עשה instead. Then they could agree that קידושין do not work with women forbidden by a לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who argue with רבי עקיבא
Unions forbidden by a negative command
Unions forbidden by a positive command
Instead of explaining it as

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
instead of setting it in those forbidden by a negative command,
phrases.notes: 'It' means the פסוק about the loved wife and the hated wife.

phrases.english: let them set it in those forbidden by a positive command!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, אַדְּמוֹקֵי לַהּ בְּחַיָּיבֵי לָאוִין, נוֹקְמַהּ בְּחַיָּיבֵי עֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי ישבב's view to the view of the רבנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's reading of the פסוק as women forbidden by a לאו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A milder case, forbidden only by an עשה, could fit the פסוק. So the פסוק does not prove that קידושין work with women forbidden by a לאו.

steps.title: No positive-command case fits the verse
steps.stepSummary: Each possible עשה case fails, so the רבנן had to use women forbidden by a לאו.
steps.simpleTranslation: These women forbidden by an עשה, which ones are they? If both wives are Egyptian converts, then both are 'hated.' If one is Egyptian and one is a regular Jewish woman, that does not work, because we need two wives from the same nation. If it is a בעולה with a כהן גדול, does the פסוק say 'if a כהן has two wives'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 17. It goes through every case forbidden by an עשה and shows that none of them fits the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both wives are Egyptian converts, neither is 'loved,' because both marriages are forbidden. If only one is Egyptian, the two wives are not from the same nation, and the פסוק needs that. A בעולה with a כהן גדול does not fit either, because the פסוק talks about any man, not a כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: An Egyptian convert woman, whom a Jew is forbidden by an עשה to marry
The 'hated' wife in the פסוק
From one nation
Is it written...? (meaning: it is not)

phrases.english: These ones forbidden by a positive command, what are they?
If both of them are Egyptian converts,
both of them are hated,
phrases.notes: Both marriages are forbidden, so there is no 'loved' wife to compare with.

phrases.english: if one is an Egyptian and one is a Jewish woman,
we need two wives from one nation,
if a non-virgin with a High Priest,
is it written 'if a priest has'?
phrases.notes: The פסוק in דברים 21:15 says 'if a man has two wives,' not 'if a כהן has.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 by ruling out every עשה case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן could have explained the 'hated wife' as a woman forbidden by an עשה.
steps.terutzMaskana: No עשה case fits the wording of the פסוק, so the רבנן explain it as women forbidden by a לאו.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the רבנן's reading of the פסוק is the natural one, and why it supports their view that קידושין work with women forbidden by a לאו.

steps.title: What about רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי עקיבא can explain the פסוק if every reasonable case fails.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same problem on רבי עקיבא. He holds that קידושין do not work with women forbidden by a לאו, so he must use a narrow case that the רבנן just rejected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We just saw that a case limited to a כהן גדול does not fit 'if a man has two wives.' Yet רבי עקיבא is left only with cases like that: a widow with a כהן גדול (according to רבי סימאי) or a בעולה with a כהן גדול (according to רבי ישבב). So how does he read the פסוק?

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva?
phrases.notes: He means: how does רבי עקיבא handle the problems we just raised against the עשה cases?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the problems from step 18 against רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's reading of the פסוק as a narrow case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The cases left for him do not fit the plain words of the פסוק.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא is forced into a difficult reading
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא has no choice. He must read the פסוק as a narrow, difficult case.
steps.simpleTranslation: You have no choice: he must leave the פסוק as a difficult reading, and it is set in its own narrow case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that רבי עקיבא's reading is forced. Because of his view, he has no other way to explain the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא holds that קידושין do not work with women forbidden by a לאו. So the 'hated wife' must be one of the narrow cases where קידושין still works, like a widow or a בעולה married to a כהן גדול, even if that is a strained reading. The גמרא accepts that he lives with this difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: Against your will; you have no choice
Forced, strained
It is set in its own case

phrases.english: You have no choice; leave the verse
phrases.notes: He means: we have to accept that this פסוק gets an unusual reading for רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: as a forced reading, and it stands on its own case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 19 by accepting a forced reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A forced reading should disprove רבי עקיבא's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of his view, רבי עקיבא has no choice but to read the פסוק as a narrow, difficult case.
steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן read the 'hated wife' as a woman forbidden by a לאו, because no עשה case fits. רבי עקיבא must accept a forced reading with a narrow case involving a כהן גדול, because he holds that קידושין do not work with women forbidden by a לאו.

steps.title: Where do we learn that קידושין fails with a שפחה כנענית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the last case of the משנה and asks for the source that קידושין does not take effect with a שפחה כנענית.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And any woman who cannot be married to him or to others, the child is like her.' From where do we know this about a שפחה כנענית?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, the case where no marriage can take effect at all. It asks for the source that a שפחה כנענית cannot receive קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the סוגיא dealt with women whose קידושין fails only with this man, like the עריות. Now the משנה's last category is women with whom קידושין does not work with anyone. The גמרא wants a פסוק showing that a שפחה כנענית belongs in this category.

keyTerms.meaning: A non-Jewish maidservant owned by a Jew
From where do we know this? (asks for a source)
Etc.; the rest of the משנה's words are understood
She cannot be married to him (her קידושין to him does not take effect)

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל מִי שֶׁאֵין לָהּ עָלָיו וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: And any woman who cannot be married to him, etc.
phrases.notes: The full line in the משנה goes on: 'or to others, the child is like her.'

phrases.english: A Canaanite maidservant, from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of רבי עקיבא and the רבנן and opens the משנה's final category.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source that קידושין does not take effect with a שפחה כנענית.

steps.title: רב הונא learns it from the donkey in the story of the עקידה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reads 'stay here with the donkey' as 'a nation similar to a donkey', showing that קידושין does not take effect with a שפחה כנענית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: the פסוק says, 'You stay here with the donkey.' Read it as 'a nation that is like a donkey.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers with a פסוק. אברהם told his servants to stay 'with the donkey', and the word for 'with' is read as 'nation'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עִם ('with') is read as עַם ('nation'). This compares אברהם's servants to the donkey in one legal way. Just as קידושין cannot take effect with an animal, it cannot take effect with a שפחה כנענית.

keyTerms.meaning: 'With' / 'nation'; same letters, read two ways
Donkey

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The verse states:
"You stay here with the donkey"
phrases.notes: בראשית 22:5. אברהם is speaking to his servants on the way to the עקידה.

phrases.english: A nation that is similar to a donkey.
phrases.notes: The word עִם ('with') is being read as עַם ('nation'). The point is only that קידושין cannot work, just as with an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'stay here with the donkey', read as 'a nation like a donkey': just as קידושין does not take effect with an animal, it does not take effect with a שפחה כנענית.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic source that a Jew's קידושין to a שפחה כנענית has no legal effect at all.

steps.title: Summing up what is proven so far, before the next question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that it has proven קידושין does not take effect with a שפחה כנענית, and gets ready to ask about the status of the child.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have found that קידושין does not take effect with her.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא lists what it has already proven so it can ask next for a source for the second half of the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said two things: there is no קידושין, and the child is like the mother. רב הונא's פסוק proved only the first part. The sentence is left open because the גמרא is about to ask where we learn that the child follows her status.

keyTerms.meaning: We have found (sums up what is proven, before asking what is still missing)
קידושין takes effect

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this line as the end of the topic. It only sums up the first half, and the גמרא is about to ask about the child.

phrases.english: We have found that betrothal does not take effect with her,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up what רב הונא proved and sets up the next question about the child's status.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Prepares to ask for a source that the child of a שפחה כנענית follows her status.
